terms.gloss: I give up, I give in
terms.grammar: dare manūs, literally to hold out one’s hands to be bound
evidence: Plaut. Pers. 854: Fateor, manūs vōbīs dō.
Hor. Epod. 17.1: Jam jam efficācī dō manūs scientiae
Cic. Att. 2.22.2: ad extrēmum autem manūs dedisse
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: manūs dare, to give the hands to be bound, and so to give up, yield, surrender. Plautus’s slave-dealer says it when he is beaten, Horace when he gives in to the witch’s art. Festus, as Lewis & Short quotes him (s.v. herba), records an older phrase from Plautus, herbam dō, “I own myself beaten”, from contests of running and strength in the meadow; it is too rare to recommend.

phrases.english: I give up; what is it?

phrases.latin: Satis sūmpsimus supplicī jam. — Fateor, manūs vōbīs dō.
phrases.english: We’ve punished him enough now. — I admit it: I give in.

phrases.latin: sī tibi vēra videntur, dēde manūs, aut, sī falsum est, accingere contrā
phrases.english: if it seems true to you, give in; or if it is false, arm yourself against it

sources: Lewis & Short: manus · Lewis & Short: herba
